html:
Serengeti National Park in northern Tanzania was set up in 1951 to protect the plains where over a million wildebeest, with zebra and gazelles, migrate in a great yearly circle between Tanzania and Kenya's Maasai Mara.

The Maasai herders who used the land were moved out of the park in 1959 to the neighbouring Ngorongoro area, a pattern of removals that still causes conflict. The German zoologist Bernhard Grzimek's film Serengeti Shall Not Die, which won an Oscar in 1960, made it famous.

UNESCO listed it in 1981. Safari tourism in the park and around Kilimanjaro is one of Tanzania's main earners, and the park is near Olduvai Gorge.
